designVerdict: SELECTED - the two channel switches (Q1, Q2), driven by the LM5069.
notes: Replaces the P-channel TM40P06D (C7422850). N-channel because the LM5069 charge pump drives the gate above the source, which is what made the high-side gate network unnecessary.

100 V against the SMAJ36CA 58.1 V clamp is 1.72x, where the 60 V P-FET sat at 1.03x - a margin this design twice called uncomfortable and twice failed to fix. Note the 60 V TPS54360B and SS36 still sit at 1.03x on the unswitched bus.
Rds(on) 9.5 mOhm MAX at Vgs 10 V (p.1) - quote this, not LCSC's 7.5 mOhm typical, in anything load-bearing. Roughly 13.3 mOhm at Tj 100 C, so 0.079 W at the 2.43 A channel current.

SOA (Fig. 12 p.4) MUST BE READ BY PIXEL. Two readings here were wrong, by 4.5x and then 1.4x. Calibrated against the curve's own Rds(on) segment (0.1 V, 13.3 A = 7.5 mOhm), the DC trace is a constant-power asymptote at ~70-75 W whose 1 A point is at 70 V; the vertical segment at 100 V is the BVdss wall, not a power line. At Vds 36 V the DC SOA allows ~72 W, so the 39.8 W power limit clears by 1.8x, falling to 1.46x at the PWR_ILM max corner. The 10 ms curve gives 171 W.

JUNCTION RISE IS VERIFIABLE, contrary to an earlier note here. Fig. 13 p.6 publishes normalised transient thermal impedance vs pulse width (single pulse plus six duty cycles) with the formula Tj,pk = Tc + Pdm x Zth-jc x Rth-jc. At the 96 ms worst-case ramp Z is about 0.45; with the figure's own Rth-jc = 4.5 C/W that is an 81 C rise, so Tj about 106 C at 25 C ambient. The datasheet contradicts itself - p.1 gives Rth-jc 0.84 C/W - and 4.5 is the pessimistic choice.
RthJA 50 C/W on 1 in2 of 2 oz copper (p.1 note 2), so about 2.5 W at 25 C ambient. Steady state is not the binding constraint; the 39.8 W ramp is, and that is transient.
Datasheet lists 'PD Charger V-BUS' as a typical application.
